title: Primer graph coalescer and token-path attribution reporter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a primer graph coalescer that reduces duplicate primer warmups and a token-path attribution reporter that breaks down latency/cost per primer edge. Improves coldstart warmup efficiency and enables edge-level hotspotting reports.
description:
Summary: Add a new workload runner helper (primer-graph-coalescer) and a companion reporter (token-path-attribution) to the benchmark lab toolkit. The coalescer groups similar primers into a compact directed graph, schedules deterministic prefetches to reduce redundant KV-cache priming, and exposes a per-edge attribution trace so we can map latency and token cost to primer transitions.
Motivation: many production prompt workloads reuse overlapping primer prefixes which leads to duplicated warmup work across sessions. Existing runners either replay primers verbatim or treat primers as opaque strings; we need a middle ground that preserves primer ordering for fidelity but collapses redundant warmup paths to reduce wasted work in CFG-style workloads.
What this PR contains:
- A primer graph builder that constructs a directed acyclic-ish graph by splitting primers on token boundary similarities and exact-match suffix/prefix heuristics. The builder is conservative: edges are only merged when overlap >= configured threshold.
- A deterministic prefetch scheduler that traverses frequent paths and issues coalesced KV-cache priming requests with backoff and headroom controls. This keeps the runtime workload close to production warmup without introducing nondeterministic interleaving.
- Token-path attribution reporter: collects tracing hooks during runner execution and aggregates latency, token counts, and memory pressure per graph edge, producing CSV and JSON reports with per-edge p50/p95/p99 metrics and a compact top-k hotspot report.
- CLI flags and config: new --primer-coalesce-threshold, --deterministic-prefetch, --edge-window-ms, and reporter.output-format.
- Integration with existing harness: the new runner mode can be selected via workload_type=primer-graph in the orchestrator.
Design notes:
- Coalescing heuristic favors false negatives over false positives to avoid changing logical primer ordering; we never reorder tokens, only collapse identical suffixes/prefixes and contiguous token-aligned overlaps.
- Prefetches are sized to respect batch size limits; coalescer emits a minimal set of prefetch sequences and the scheduler batches those across tenants up to configured concurrency.
- Attribution traces attach lightweight edge IDs to requests; they do not change model inputs and are scrubbed before persistence.
Performance observations (local perf-canary runs):
- With a synthetic dataset derived from production primer samples (N=25k sessions), coalescing threshold=0.7 reduced redundant primer priming traffic by ~34% and reduced median coldstart-latency for 1st user token by ~18%.
- Deterministic prefetch added a negligible 2.2% overhead to steady-state qps but reduced p95 coldstart latency variance by ~41%.
- Token-path reporter introduced ~1.6% additional CPU on the harness side but produced high-signal hotspot maps that correlated with kernel-level flamepoints.
How to run (examples):
- Build: make -C benchmark-lab all && ./bin/benchctl runner --workload primer-graph --config configs/primer_graph.yaml
- Produce report: ./bin/benchctl report --input runs/<id> --reporter token-path-attribution --output reports/<id>.json
Backwards compatibility & safety:
- Existing workloads (session-replay, seq-batch) are unaffected unless workload_type=primer-graph is selected.
- All new flags are opt-in and default to conservative values.
- Sensitive primer text is hashed for graph matching and attribution reports only reference edge IDs; raw primer text is not stored in reports.
